[IMAGE] This image illustrates the concept of a vector area element in the context of surface integrals, often used in electromagnetism and fluid dynamics.

The top part of the image shows a small flat surface area, labeled as ΔS, with a unit normal vector (denoted by \(\hat{n}\)) perpendicular to the surface. The equation ΔS = ΔS \(\hat{n}\) indicates that the area element ΔS can be represented as a vector by multiplying the scalar area ΔS by the unit normal vector \(\hat{n}\).

The bottom part of the image depicts a curved surface where a small patch of the surface, ΔS, is highlighted with its corresponding unit normal vector \(\hat{n}\), showing that the same vector representation of the area element applies to curved surfaces as well.
Source: NCERT Grade 12 Physics, Page 22

[IMAGE] This image illustrates the concept of electric field lines due to a charged spherical conductor. It shows a cross-section of a smaller charged sphere (with radius \( r \)) placed at the center of a larger spherical shell (with radius \( R \)).

The smaller sphere has a positive charge, which influences the electric field lines radiating outward uniformly in all directions. The labeled parts, \( r \) and \( R \), represent the radii of the inner charged sphere and the outer spherical boundary, respectively, while the arrows labeled \( r \) and \( R \) indicate the direction of the electric field lines from the positively charged sphere to the outer boundary. This setup helps in understanding how electric fields behave around charged conductors and the concept of electric flux through a Gaussian surface.

[IMAGE] This image depicts a microwave oven, a common household appliance used to heat or cook food quickly using microwave radiation. In the context of an NCERT Grade 12 Physics textbook, it likely illustrates the concept of how microwave ovens utilize electromagnetic waves, specifically microwaves, to transfer energy to water molecules in food, thereby generating heat.

The labeled parts, such as the control panel and the interior cooking chamber, highlight the areas where users interact with the device and where the microwaving process occurs. The control panel allows users to set the time and power level, which are crucial for regulating the microwave radiation emitted inside the oven. The image helps students understand the practical application of electromagnetic waves in everyday technology.
